impl.summary: Comfy-Org's NVIDIA VFX Nodes 0.2.1 (pinned at 38d790d) now drive three new choices on the open engine. 'Quick · RTX' is RTX Video Super Resolution in Upscale → Video. 'RTX Frame Generation' (RTX 40 series or newer) is in FPS boost. 'RTX Video HDR' (HLG or HDR10/PQ) is in SDR to HDR. Each choice has its own hand-built ComfyUI graph and pre-flight board row. The GPU pre-flight reads the card's name, so the board, chips, guided fix and run check say 'Needs an NVIDIA RTX card' (or 'RTX 40 series or newer') on CPU, Apple, AMD, Intel and GTX devices. Nothing is picked automatically and today's defaults are unchanged. Upscale → Video shows Quick · RTX next to Restore · faithful and Regenerate · creative: first on an RTX card, switched off with the reason on a card that can't run it, and last when the card is unknown. The cloud has no RTX route because nobody hosts NVIDIA's SDK. Nothing was built before this package: no RTX graph, pack, model or readiness check existed at fdad177c. The brief was out of date in two places: the installer did not already know the platform (it installs CPU PyTorch; I added nvidia-smi detection), and the licence is stated (pack Apache-2.0, nvidia-vfx runtime proprietary under NVIDIA's Software License Agreement).
built: Library: three hand-built graphs. upscale-video-rtx works in VHS meta-batch passes like upscale-video-esrgan-chunked, keeps the sound, scales by min(4, max(1, shortSide / the shorter edge)) worked out in the graph, then resizes to exactly shortSide. fps-rtx-framegen is interpolate-rife-fps with RTXVideoFrameGeneration in FrameInterpolate's place (m and every n-th frame, shot-change detection on, last frame held so N becomes N×m+1). sdr-to-hdr-rtx is RTXTrueHDR into CreateVideo 10-bit, with one colorSpace binding feeding both output_colorspace and color_space so the H.264 High 10 tags always match (bt2020 + arib-std-b67 or smpte2084). All three are in library.spec.mjs with packs, licence and notes, plus manifest, requirements.json and validation-state.json.

New spec field gpu (nvidia-rtx / nvidia-rtx-40), carried through build-library.mjs into manifest.json and through build-requirements.mjs into requirements.json. New binding key rtxQuality. PACK_CLASSES and CUSTOM_NODE_REPOS entries. object_info.subset.json gains only the three RTX classes, as null.

Node pack: ComfyUI_Nvidia_VFX_Nodes is in workflows/comfyui/packs.json (registry id comfyui_nvidia_rtx_nodes, requirementsTxt true). install-comfyui.sh clones it and installs nvidia-vfx==0.2.0.0 only when nvidia-smi names an RTX or GB10 card (RTX_VIDEO=1 forces it, RTX_VIDEO=0 skips it), and warns when PyTorch is not a CUDA 13 build. scripts/comfy/README.md has a new section on these graphs.

Licences as information: a NODE_PACKS row for the pack (Apache-2.0) with a note on the NVIDIA runtime. The 'NVIDIA Software License Agreement' is recognised as a licence with conditions, so the workflows show under that class in Settings → Models & licences. The research table row in new-models-10.md is corrected.

src/lib/gpu/rtx.ts (readCard, cardFits, offerOn, GPU_NEED_TEXT) reads RTX cards and their series from ComfyUI device names. It covers GeForce, RTX A-series, Ada and Blackwell pro cards, Quadro and TITAN RTX, and GB10; AMD, ROCm, Apple, Intel, CPU and GTX read as not RTX; data-centre names read as unknown and are never blocked.

Readiness: workflowReadiness returns unsupported with the reason and gpuNeed. Badge flags 8 and 16 make the chip read 'RTX only' or 'RTX 40+'. stateLine, the header pill, the guided-fix title and body, and a separate board summary sentence all say the card is needed. FixPlan carries reason and gpuNeed. An RTX graph never reads 'Runs on any computer'. The run gate stops an RTX run on a card that can't run it, with a plain message.

Catalog: src/lib/catalog/rtx-video.ts (ids, copy, rtxStanding, RTX_MISSING). Three open models: oss-rtx-video-upscale (Source control), oss-rtx-frame-generation (Quality control, fps targets and slow motion) and oss-rtx-video-hdr (HLG and PQ formats, peak 400-2000 nits). They come after each tool's own models, are open only, and studio defaults are unchanged.

UI: FinishChoices adds Quick · RTX. It is first on a fitting card, last when the card is unknown, and switched off (aria-disabled) with 'Needs an NVIDIA RTX card' otherwise. Three choices sit in 3 columns on desktop, and on a phone the first takes a row of its own. A line under the picked choice says it runs only on NVIDIA RTX cards. FPS boost and SDR to HDR offer the RTX models through the model picker, whose taglines say RTX.

Pre-flight board (/connect): three new rows ('Quick upscale · RTX', 'FPS boost · RTX', 'SDR to HDR · RTX'). Canvas: an Upscale node entry 'Quick upscale (RTX)', switched off on the cloud, with no cloud stand-in (GPU_ONLY_FIXED).

Provider: RTX passes are sized by RTX's own scale, not ESRGAN's 4x. RTXVideoFrameGeneration is linked out when m is 1. A ComfyUI without the nodes gets plain words, one version for the owner and one for visitors.
impl.tests: New tests/rtx-video.test.ts, 21 tests, all passing. It checks each graph's RTX node inputs against the pack's define_schema at 38d790d; chunk sizes and scale (rtxScale, rtxOutputSize, framesPerPass, and the provider's framesPerBatch, shortSide and quality); frame counts ((N-1)M+1, and N×m+1 matching RIFE's fpsFrames); m/n and the link-out; that both HDR colour tags are always equal in HLG and PQ, and that EXR is refused; the GPU names; readiness on CPU, --cpu, AMD, GTX, Apple, H100 and RTX 3090 vs 4070; badge text and stateLine; rtxStanding; that models are open only and defaults unchanged; board rows; the Canvas entry and its missing cloud stand-in; licences; and the missing-nodes message. Added the three ids to the unvalidated list in tests/comfy-library-4.test.ts (the allowed edit). Live check on the CPU ComfyUI: the graphs with core stand-ins in place of the RTX nodes (ImageScaleBy, ImageSDRToHDR) ran end to end. 3 s 320x180 25 fps with sound became 1280x720, 75 frames in 5 passes, AAC kept; the HDR graph wrote H.264 High 10 yuv420p10le tagged bt2020/arib-std-b67 (HLG) and smpte2084 (PQ), sound kept. validate-workflows records missing_node_type for the three graphs, as expected. Browser check with tests/e2e/rtx-video.mjs (demo mode, port 3461, 1440 and 390 px, light and dark, stubbed GPU answers for unknown, RTX 4070 and AMD cards): all 104 checks passed, with no console or page errors, no hydration filter and no sideways scroll; .next deleted after. npx next typegen 0, pnpm typecheck 0, pnpm lint 0 (one existing warning, WAN_NEG_EN). Full vitest (--maxWorkers=2) exit 1: 8 failed out of 4982. Six are the known rule-8 failures: dop-originals, split-soundtrack, soul-runs ×2, comfy-reuse, preset-featured. The other two, picker-covers and preset-covers, are rule-12 timeouts and passed when rerun alone (36/36).
left: Nothing has run on an NVIDIA RTX card. Validate on a ComfyUI with the pack and an RTX card: node scripts/comfy/validate-workflows.mjs upscale-video-rtx fps-rtx-framegen sdr-to-hdr-rtx, then a real run of each. The things to confirm are the DynamicCombo nested keys (resize_type.scale, generation_type.multiplier) taking a link, VRAM use, and speed.

Needs on a GPU host: a CUDA 13 (cu130) PyTorch, which install-comfyui.sh does not install (it installs CPU wheels; it only warns), and NVIDIA driver 570.190+ / 580.82+ / 590.44+ on Linux. nvidia-vfx 0.2.0.0 ships wheels for Linux x86_64 and Windows only, so DGX Spark (Linux arm64) has no wheel even though the pack's README says Spark is supported.
tests/comfy-library-4.test.ts: the unvalidated list now names upscale-video-rtx, fps-rtx-framegen and sdr-to-hdr-rtx (the only allowed edit).

Not built: EXR and ProRes output for the RTX HDR path. EXR stays on video-sdr-to-hdr-exr, and the model refuses exr. The brief's 'encode HDR10 / ProRes' is covered as HDR10 = PQ in 10-bit H.264, the existing export path's colorSpace.

Hosted runs (FUOBE_HOSTED_RUNS): RTX models go through the existing decidePlace and poolAllows unchanged, and video inputs usually keep them on the account's own GPU. The run gate stops them on an install card that isn't RTX. No pool-specific RTX rule and no hosted-runs test were added.
'Fast preview tier' for n7-3 and archive-restore: the upscale-video-rtx graph and the oss-rtx-video-upscale model are ready to reuse, but nothing is wired into those packages.

Owner decision still open: should Quick · RTX become the default on RTX hosts? The brief says to keep today's default unless the owner chooses, so SeedVR2 stays the default and RTX is only placed first.
impl.docsNotes: ARCHITECTURE: library 204 → 207 workflows and one node pack (ComfyUI_Nvidia_VFX_Nodes @38d790d, registry comfyui_nvidia_rtx_nodes, Apache-2.0, with the NVIDIA nvidia-vfx 0.2.0.0 runtime under the NVIDIA Software License Agreement). The graphs are upscale-video-rtx (upscale-video), fps-rtx-framegen (interpolate) and sdr-to-hdr-rtx (sdr-to-hdr). New spec, manifest and requirements field gpu (nvidia-rtx / nvidia-rtx-40), read by src/lib/gpu/rtx.ts and checked in workflowReadiness (state unsupported, gpuNeed, badge flags 8/16). New binding key rtxQuality. install-comfyui.sh RTX_VIDEO=auto|1|0. FEATURES and SELF-HOSTING (docs pass): Upscale → Video 'Quick · RTX', FPS boost 'RTX Frame Generation' (RTX 40+), SDR to HDR 'RTX Video HDR' (HLG or HDR10) run only on NVIDIA RTX cards with a CUDA 13 PyTorch; the pre-flight says 'Needs an NVIDIA RTX card' elsewhere; there is no cloud version. STATUS: the three graphs are not validated (they need an RTX card).

findings.summary: Hosted runs (FUOBE_HOSTED_RUNS=1) never check the card for the RTX models. decidePlace puts a pool run on the install's own ComfyUI without asking whether that card is an NVIDIA RTX one, and the generations route skips gateGeneration for every pool run ('its plan was checked by decidePlace'). So the new gpuNeed stop never runs on that path. Take an account with no GPU online (or wish 'pool'), a policy that allows video uploads, and an install GPU that isn't RTX or lacks the pack: picking Quick · RTX / RTX Frame Generation / RTX Video HDR gets a quote and a hold, then fails inside ComfyUI with missing_node_type or a CUDA error. ownGpu() is unset on the pool, so promptRefusal returns RTX_MISSING.owner, and that text names scripts/comfy/install-comfyui.sh and RTX_VIDEO=1 to an account (the brief bans file names and jargon in visitor copy). The brief asked for these models to plan and price on the pool path with a test in the style of tests/hosted-runs.test.ts. None was added (the implementer says so in 'left'). Hosted runs are off by default, hence medium.
findings.verified: Traced: route.ts:162 `if (viewer.kind !== "guest" && !onPool)` wraps the only gateGeneration call; hosted-run.ts decidePlace and poolAllows have no card/gpu check; comfyui.ts promptRefusal picks RTX_MISSING.owner when !ownGpu().

findings.summary: The guided-fix body for an RTX tool puts the raw device name into visitor copy. Both callers fill plan.gpu with deviceLabel(dev.name): gate.ts:90 always, and readiness-service.ts:135 whenever vram_total is set, which ComfyUI also sets to system RAM on a CPU. ComfyUI names the CPU device 'cpu' and Apple's 'mps', so a CPU or Mac visitor reads '…which only NVIDIA RTX cards have, and your cpu isn't one' / 'your mps isn't one'. The older GpuState copy avoids this because it only names the card when haveGb is set, and haveGb is undefined on a CPU. The closing sentence 'The other choices in this tool work on your GPU' is also not true on a CPU, or where the other choices need a bigger GPU. Fix: drop the name unless the device type is cuda/xpu (or use summary.gpu, which is only set for real GPUs), and soften or drop the last sentence.
findings.verified: Read deviceLabel (the strip regex needs whitespace after 'cpu'/'mps', so a bare 'cpu' comes back unchanged), gate.ts:90, readiness-service.ts:134-135 and guided-fix.tsx:159-166.

findings.summary: GB10 (DGX Spark) reads as a fitting RTX card (series 50), so readiness says it fits and Quick · RTX goes first, and the installer auto-installs the pack there. But pypi.nvidia.com has no linux aarch64 wheel of nvidia-vfx 0.2.0.0, only manylinux x86_64, win_amd64 and win_arm64. On a Spark the install fails, and the tool shows as one setup step away when it can never run. The pack's README does claim 'RTX Spark is supported', and the implementer flagged the gap in 'left'. Until a wheel exists, readCard should treat GB10 as unknown (never first, never blocked) rather than as fitting.
findings.verified: Listed https://pypi.nvidia.com/nvidia-vfx/: there are 0.2.0.0 wheels for cp310, cp311 and cp312-abi3 manylinux x86_64 and win_amd64, plus win_arm64 for cp311 and cp312, and nothing for aarch64.

findings.summary: Keyboard use of the switched-off choice. radioKeys walks '[role="radio"]:not([disabled])', but Quick · RTX is only aria-disabled, so on a card that can't run it the arrow keys land on it and 'click' it: nothing is picked and focus rests on a choice that is switched off. Not a trap (the next arrow moves on), and ARIA allows focusable disabled radios. Skipping aria-disabled in radioKeys would match how a mouse user experiences it.

checks: Read the review prompt and main-rules. Branch o/nm10-rtx-video at 7b0c3573, worktree clean before and after. I diffed fdad177c...HEAD over 37 files and reviewed the changes with the code around them.

Primary sources: I cloned Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_Nvidia_VFX_Nodes. HEAD = 38d790d (the pin), pyproject name comfyui_nvidia_rtx_nodes 0.2.1, LICENSE Apache-2.0, requirements.txt 'nvidia-vfx>=0.2'. Through range reads of the 443 MB wheel's zip directory I confirmed it ships NVIDIA-Software-License-Agreement-2025.05.05.pdf, product-specific-terms-for-nvidia-ai-products-2025.05.05.pdf and NVIDIA-Open-Model-License-Agreements-24-10-2025.pdf. The driver minimums 570.190+/580.82+/590.44+ (Linux) and 570.65 (Windows) match the package metadata. The licence data recorded in the spec, licences.ts NODE_PACKS and KNOWN, and new-models-10.md is accurate.

Graphs: hand-built and workflows/ copies are the same (differences only in number formatting, 1.0 vs 1). Checked against object_info.subset.json: CreateVideo color_space takes HDR / HDR PQ with bit_depth 10, ComfyMathExpression outputs FLOAT, ImageFromBatch takes -1, and the VHS_VideoInfo outputs 5/8/9 are loaded fps/width/height. The colorSpace binding feeds both RTXTrueHDR.output_colorspace and CreateVideo.color_space. fps-rtx-framegen keeps interpolate-rife-fps's node ids, and the bypass now also finds RTXVideoFrameGeneration.

FinishChoices puts Quick · RTX first only when offerOn says the card fits. It is switched off with 'Needs an NVIDIA RTX card' when the chip has flag 8/16 or the name reads non-RTX, and goes last but stays enabled when the card is unknown. composer pickModel resets params to the new model's defaults, so the HDR peakNits minimum of 200 doesn't carry over to RTX's 400. review.verdict: approve with fixes: the work matches the brief, and the licences and node schemas check out against the primary sources. Nothing is auto-picked, and the pre-flight and UI say plainly that an NVIDIA RTX card is needed. Before FINISH, fix the hosted-run gap (the pool path skips the card check, and it can show the owner's missing-pack message to an account) or record it as a known limitation, and fix the 'your cpu isn't one' wording in the guided fix. The rest is low.

applied: Medium (hosted runs, confirmed): the pool path now checks the install's card before it plans an RTX model. New poolCardRefuses(modelId) in src/server/hosted-run.ts reads the install's last GPU check. It refuses Quick · RTX, RTX Frame Generation or RTX Video HDR when gpuFits says the card can't run it (CPU, Apple, AMD, Intel, GTX, or an RTX 20/30 card for frame generation) or when the check lists any RTX Video node class as missing. decidePlace refuses after poolAllows (403 not-offered) with the new HOSTED_WORDS.rtxCard line: 'This one needs an NVIDIA RTX card, and this studio's GPUs can't run it right now. Connect your own GPU in Settings, or pick another choice.' When the account has its own GPU and didn't ask for the pool, the run goes to its own GPU instead, where the existing gate applies. poolQuote returns null, so the price check never quotes it on the pool. Nothing reaches /v1/quote or /v1/reserve. A card the name doesn't identify (data-centre cards), or no check yet, is never refused (R11). RTX_CLASSES is exported from src/lib/catalog/rtx-video.ts.

Owner copy never reaches an account: promptRefusal in src/server/providers/comfyui.ts now uses the visitor wording when ownGpu() or tenantAccount() is set, so hosted runs inside runOnPool are covered. This applies to RTX_MISSING and also to the same pattern in REGEN_COPY, which named install-comfyui.sh and OPEN_H3_REGEN to pool accounts.

The guided-fix closing sentence 'The other choices in this tool work on your GPU' is now 'Pick another choice in this tool for this clip.'

Low (GB10, confirmed by the reviewer's pypi.nvidia.com listing): readCard reads GB10 as unknown (never put first, never blocked). install-comfyui.sh auto mode now matches only 'RTX' and skips machines that aren't x86_64, because nvidia-vfx 0.2.0.0 has no Linux arm64 wheel. RTX_VIDEO=1 still forces the install. The tests are updated to match.
Low (radioKeys): the arrow keys now skip [aria-disabled="true"] radios as well as [disabled] ones, so a switched-off Quick · RTX is no longer landed on and 'clicked'.

fix.finalSummary: nm10-rtx-video is ready for FINISH. Open engine (ComfyUI): Quick · RTX (Upscale → Video), RTX Frame Generation (FPS boost, RTX 40+) and RTX Video HDR (HLG or HDR10/PQ) are built as three hand-built graphs with the Comfy-Org NVIDIA VFX pack pinned at 38d790d (Apache-2.0; the nvidia-vfx runtime is under NVIDIA's Software License Agreement, shown as information). Graph inputs are checked against the pack's schema, and core stand-ins ran on the CPU ComfyUI. Nothing has run on a real RTX card: that needs an NVIDIA RTX GPU, a CUDA 13 PyTorch and a recent driver. The pre-flight, chips, guided fix and run gate say 'Needs an NVIDIA RTX card' (or 'RTX 40 series or newer') on CPU, Apple, AMD, Intel and GTX devices, and never name a bare cpu or mps device. Nothing is auto-picked and today's defaults are unchanged. GB10 / DGX Spark now reads as unknown and the installer skips it, since there is no arm64 runtime. Cloud engine: no route, because nobody hosts NVIDIA's SDK; the Canvas entry is switched off on the cloud. No key is needed. Public sign-up: guests browse as before. Accounts run these on their own GPU with the existing gate. With hosted runs on (FUOBE_HOSTED_RUNS=1), an account's RTX run on the install's GPUs is refused in plain words before any quote or hold when the install's card can't run it or lacks the nodes. Where it does run there, a missing-nodes failure shows the visitor's words, never the owner's script or switch names.
